verification.note: At the reviewed worktree, addons/intelligence/frontend/ScenesSection/ScenesSectionContainer.tsx:482-486 runs the `enter` branch (activate(browseRef.current) when non-null) before `if (list.length === 0) return;`. In the main checkout (/Users/libre/Sources/video_share, taken to be the base) the same handler has the guard at line 470, before the Enter branch at 472. So Enter on a `.loft` with no candidate rows now seeks to the browse point, and before this change it did nothing. Native videos cannot reach this path: view is 'expanded' only when nativeState === 'ready' (lines 579-583), which is set only when next.length > 0 (lines 235, 256-262), and useRulerKeys is enabled only when view === 'expanded' (line 636). The touch-point text for the container says only 'no change list, no mode' and does not name the keyboard change. I4 specifies click seeks but says nothing about keyboard. The behavior is pinned by ScenesSectionOneList.test.tsx:464-492 (arrows and Home/End do nothing; Enter seeks about 50 s).

specification_compliance: I4 specifies seeking on a click at a fraction of the ruler. Enter-to-seek on an empty-candidate `.loft` goes beyond the text but fits the same intent (ScenesSectionContainer.tsx:482-486).
potential_unspecified_behavior: Enter on the ruler of a `.loft` with no candidate rows now seeks to the browse point; neither the touch points nor I4 name this (ScenesSectionContainer.tsx:482-486).
regression_risks: The keyboard path for an empty list changed order; native videos cannot reach it because the ruler keys are bound only in the 'expanded' view, which needs at least one row.
test_coverage: ScenesSectionOneList.test.tsx:464-492 covers hover browse, arrows/Home/End as no-ops, and Enter seeking on an empty-candidate `.loft`.
not_verified: The base was not read through git: the pre-change line order comes from the main checkout at /Users/libre/Sources/video_share, which may not be exactly origin/develop.
The other touch points (backend handler, i18n keys, e2e fixtures) were not reviewed beyond this finding.
